speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To understand what is happening, please tell me: how many days have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any changes in your urination such as frequency, urgency, or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your sinus symptoms improved but you still have fatigue, fever, and flank pain, it is possible the infection has spread to your kidneys. Can you describe the color or clarity of your urine, and do you see any blood in it? Also, have you had any recent travel or exposure to untreated water?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present, Bacterial_Culture: Negative, Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel’s_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Patient
text:
The sinus symptoms improved, but the flank pain and fever stayed. The rash happened during the antibiotics and then resolved after the change in medication.
DIAGNOSIS READY: No significant finding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detail; the rash appearing during antibiotic treatment is a crucial clue. Did you notice if the rash was accompanied by joint pain or if your urine appears dark or tea-colored?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential
REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis.

The temporal relationship between your new symptoms and the antibiotic use, combined with the rash and the absence of urinary sediment on your normal urinalysis and blood work, strongly points to an allergic kidney reaction rather than a bacterial infection like pyelonephritis or a systemic reaction like SLE.
